source_scope: Frozen owned insertion implementation/tests, original assertion mapping sources, and compiled native fixture. Root integration supplies whole-workspace dependency closure. No global completion ledger changed.
behavior_fixed: Insertion now allocates and default-constructs an appended tail slot before shifting, then publishes Size before assignment. Previously it appended the supplied value without ever calling Default.
Invalid signed or unsigned indices are checked before allocation, Default, shifting, or copy/move assignment.
Borrowed before/after overloads perform Clone::clone_from on the insertion slot after Default and shifts. They do not eagerly clone the input.

Explicit assignment callbacks reproduce user-defined native move/copy operations in descending shift order; panics retain the size and exactly the completed assignment prefix. All slots remain initialized.

native_fixture.joined_columns: Event sequence, allocation-before-default order, constructor/assignment failure point, final Size, external move-source state, every final element value.
native_fixture.allocation_observation: Native derived allocator logs AllocateOptimal. Rust observes real BaseAllocator::accumulating block alloc_count deltas during Default; no fake allocator or synthesized expected allocation count. Covered fixture has no intervening element deallocations.
native_fixture.value_operation_dispatch: Native Item move assignment sets donor=-7; Rust explicit callback performs the same value operation. Custom copy/default failures are injected in those value operations at the matching native stage. Generic Rust moves are not relabeled C++ move assignment.
native_fixture.scratch_probe_scope: The preliminary scratch probe had ten insertion rows and two protected engine observations. This committed fixture contains twelve insertion rows: added before_first_move and after_negative; protected observations were not claimed ported.

original_assertion_audit.faithfulness: All native initial values, insertion indices, final Length/Size and every element assertion remain in the existing Rust mappings. Negative guards preserve ArrayError::Index classification; previous receipt maps this to Standard_OutOfRange.
original_assertion_audit.type_adaptation: Rust MoveOnly reproduces original values and non-Clone capability; it has no implicit user-defined move assignment. Supplemental explicit hook tests now verify custom move/default/failure behavior separately.

safety_and_miri: No unsafe code added. Same-block references use a slice split at destination offset; cross-block references use Vec::split_at_mut on the owning block vector.

Miri runs all nine new tests successfully. The accumulating allocator emits its pre-existing integer-to-pointer provenance warning at allocator/block.rs:46; this is not claimed strict-provenance verification of the allocator.

A separate MIRIFLAGS=-Zmiri-strict-provenance run passes the new heap-storage success/failure test at increments1,2,4, covering both same-block and cross-block shifts independently of the accumulating allocator.

Callback panic leaves initialized values owned by their original allocation slots; normal Rust destruction remains enabled. Callbacks receive distinct mutable references and can expose no dangling references in safe Rust.
remaining_partial_parity: Convenience owned and borrowed methods use Rust mem::swap shifts; these do not invoke custom C++ move operations. Users porting such value types must supply the explicit operation hooks. Generic custom destructor traces and Rust moved-input Drop timing remain adaptations.
Same-container input aliasing is not accepted through forged simultaneous references. A future index-based alias adapter needs native probes, including source mutation during descending shifts.

The generic Clone::clone_from contract may fall back to clone-and-replace. Exact native copy assignment is established only when the value operation itself is ported, as in the fixture override or explicit callback.

Protected raw block APIs, setUsedSize, arbitrary item-size allocation, constructAt/destroyAt/replaceAt capability dispatch, and raw lifetime setters remain unported; they need a separate initialized-range ownership model.
Native copyDate partial-block exception leaks versus Rust cleanup and the cursor lifetime/comparison limitations remain as documented in previous scoped receipts.
Supplemental fixtures prove the specified bounded operations and failure prefixes, not complete DynamicArray class, template instantiation, or global API parity.
